changes.after: The word `move` lets this closure take ownership of the String it uses.

before: move makes a closure capture values by value. Capturing a String transfers ownership into the closure, so the original binding can no longer use it. Capturing a Copy value instead copies it.

A move closure is not automatically callable only once. This closure merely borrows its owned String to read len, so it can be called repeatedly. A closure that moves its captured String out would instead consume that capture when called.
Expected output or behavior: 4 4. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Capture a small Copy integer and compare which original bindings remain usable. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

before.question: If main prints text after constructing length and before calling it, what happens?
choices: The closure is always called exactly once.
Compilation rejects use of text after its ownership moved into the closure.
The original text remains available because len only reads it.
before.explanation: move transferred the String at closure creation even though each later call only borrows the captured value.

after.question: Can main print the original text directly after the move?
choices: Yes. Move makes a second String.
No. The closure now owns it.
Yes. The text moved only after the first call.
after.explanation: Creating the closure moves the String into it before either call runs.
